rows.reasoning: 4 has two square roots, 2 and -2, so statement 1 is false. The real cube root of -8 is -2, so statement 2 is true. The principal fourth root of 16 is 2, so statement 3 is false. A negative number has no real fourth root, so statement 4 is false. The real fifth root of -7 is -√[5]{7}, so statement 5 is true. Thus two options are correct.

The argument is (x-1)/2, so the domain is x>1, the vertical asymptote is x=1, it passes through (3,0), and it is increasing. A horizontal/vertical translate of log_(1/2)(x) remains decreasing, so statement ⑤ is the false one.
2^(x+2)+3 is increasing on [-2,2]. Its minimum is at p=-2 and m=2^0+3=4, hence p+m=2.
4π/3 radians equals 240°, so ㄱ is true. A ray determines a directed angle only modulo full turns, so ㄴ is false. 360°n+120° is always coterminal with 120° in quadrant II, so ㄷ is true.
The base requires x+1>0 and x+1≠1, so x>-1 and x≠0. The argument requires 42-x-x²>0, equivalent to -7<x<6. The integers satisfying both are 1,2,3,4,5, giving 5.
Taking log base 7 gives 1/x=log₇a, 1/(2y)=log₇b, and 1/(3z)=log₇c. The requested sum is 6(log₇a+log₇b+log₇c)=6log₇(abc)=6log₇49=12.
log₄9=(1/2)log₂9=log₂3. Thus x=log₂6+log₂3=log₂18, so 2^x=18.
The sum telescopes: Σ log₃((k+3)/(k+2))=log₃((n+3)/3). Setting this to 2 gives (n+3)/3=9 and n=24.

Equating powers of 2 gives 2/m+1/n=3/4. Since m,n≥2, m=3 yields n=12 and m-n=-9; m=4 yields n=4 and difference 0, while m≥5 gives no integral solution. The minimum is -9, which is absent from the listed choices.
For n>0, a^n>b^n implies a>b. If b>1 then a>b>1, proving ㄴ. If ab<1 and b≥1, then a>b≥1 would force ab>1, contradiction; hence 0<b<1, proving ㄷ. ㄱ fails for a=2,b=1/2.
Symmetry about the y-axis means 4θ≡π-θ (mod 2π), so 5θ=(2k+1)π. For 0<θ<π this gives θ=π/5 or 3π/5. Arc length is 5θ, whose maximum is 3π.

a²<a implies 0<a<1, and a<b. Since a^t decreases in t, a^a>a^b, so ㄱ is true. For base a∈(0,1) and b>a, logₐb is not always greater than 1 (it is negative when b>1), so ㄴ is false. Since b+1>1, log_(b+1)a<0 and log_(b+1)(a+1)>0, so their product is negative and ㄷ is true.
The semicircle radius is 4. Arc BP=4π/3 gives central angle BOP=π/3, hence AOP=2π/3. Chord AP=8sin(π/3)=4√3 and ∠PAQ=π/6. Sector APQ area is (1/2)(4√3)²(π/6)=4π.
Let t=2^x>0. Then k=t+1+4/t, whose minimum is 5 at t=2. There are two positive t solutions exactly when k>5. Integers with |k|<10 and k>5 are 6,7,8,9, so there are 4.

The conditions give x=216^a=6^(3a) and y=216^(b/2)=6^(3b/2). Cubing the second condition yields xy=6^60, so 2a+b=40. With a,b integers greater than 2, a=3,...,18 and b=40-2a≥3, giving 16 ordered pairs.

At an intersection, k=2^(3^|x-1|+2)-x. On 0<x<1 this decreases continuously from 32 to 7; on 1<x<2 it increases continuously from 7 to 30. Both roots exist exactly for integer k in (7,30), namely 8 through 29, totaling 22.
Let a=2^(1/3), so x=a+a⁻¹ and x³=a³+3a+3a⁻¹+a⁻³=5/2+3x. Therefore 2x³-6x-2=3.

After shifting right by m, the original graph is y=log_(1/3)(k(x-m)); reflecting in y=x gives y=m+(1/k)3^(-x). The horizontal asymptote gives m=-3. Passing through (1,0) gives 0=-3+1/(3k), so k=1/9 and k+m=-26/9.

Write a=3^t with t≤3. Then a^(log₃4)=4^t=2^(2t). For this to be an integer power of 2, 2t is an integer; the admissible nonnegative exponents are 0 through 6 (including exponent 0 does not change the product). The corresponding a values multiply to 3^(0+1/2+1+3/2+2+5/2+3)=3^(21/2).
On 1<x<9, the product (x-1)(9-x) is a downward quadratic with maximum at its midpoint x=5, where it equals 16. Thus the logarithmic maximum is log₂16=4.

After n years the debt/equity ratio is 4(0.9/1.2)^n=4(3/4)^n. At n=4 the ratio is 324/256>1, while at n=5 it is 972/1024<1, so the first year when equity exceeds debt is year 5. The rounded supplied logs give log(4)=0.60 and log(4/3)=0.12, placing the threshold at n>5 by approximation; that approximation is too coarse at this boundary and disagrees with the exact ratio.
Put A=log₂n. The quadratic factors as (t-3)(t-(A-1))<0 for t=log₂x, requiring n<16 and n/2<x<8. Counting integer x gives exactly two solutions only for n=10 or 11; their sum is 21.
